Inference · framework · 2026-11-13

What does it mean to get more from every chip?

A framework for measuring inference efficiency across latency, throughput and cost per completed task.

On this page

01 · Start with the workload02 · Measure the service03 · Count completed work04 · Keep the evidence

01 · Start with the workload

The unit of comparison is a workload. Fix the model, the request mix and the quality requirements before comparing configurations. Record the hardware, concurrency, prompt length and output length so a result can be read in context.

02 · Measure the service

Track time to first token and time per output token alongside throughput, and report tail latency at the target load. A higher token rate is useful only while requests still finish within the service's latency budget.

03 · Count completed work

Cost per completed task brings compute, retries and quality into one account. For a fixed workload, divide serving cost by the number of requests that meet both the quality and the latency criteria.

04 · Keep the evidence

Record the baseline, the candidate, the test conditions and any regressions. Repeat the comparison before promoting a candidate, and use the accepted configuration as the baseline for the next round.

This work runs underneath Zenith Tokens.
